literal: If appearing, with fame let one appear; those without that, than appearing, not appearing is good.
translation: If you appear in this world, appear with fame. For those who lack it, it is better not to appear at all than to appear.
modern: ஒருவர் உலகில் பிறந்து வாழ்ந்தால் புகழோடு வாழ வேண்டும். அந்தப் புகழ் இல்லாதவர்கள் உலகில் தோன்றுவதை விடத் தோன்றாமல் இருப்பதே நல்லது.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute value of fame in human life. The word 'தோன்று' (appear) is used here to mean coming into existence or stepping onto the public stage of life. The poet declares that if one is to be born or make an appearance in the world, it must be accompanied by fame. For those who lack such fame, the text starkly states that non-existence is far better than existing without renown.
